1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user is bringing up PSRAM on BK7258 (openvela/NuttX RTOS) following a 5-stage peripheral bring-up workflow defined in `.claude/agents/velapet-peripheral-bringup.agent.md`. The PSRAM is the #1 blocker: AP side only has 336KB SRAM, insufficient for dual-screen dual-buffer and camera frame buffer (GC2145 640×480 YUYV ~614KB). The work is structured in stages S1-S4, with the user testing between each stage. All code must have English comments, pass checkpatch (0 errors, line width ≤78), and follow NuttX conventions. ARMino SDK (Apache-2.0) is the reference for register-level porting. GPL code is strictly forbidden.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - BK7258: dual-core Armv8-M STAR-MC1 SoC with PSRAM controller at 0x46080000
   - PSRAM data window at 0x60000000 (64MB address space)
   - Analog registers (ana_reg* at 0x440101xx) use serial SPI bus — must poll ANA_SPI_STATE_REG (0x440100E8) after each write
   - AHB power domain: pwd_ahbp = bit[5] of cpu_power_sleep_wakeup @ 0x44010040
   - PSRAM clock gate: psram_cken = bit[19] of cpu_device_clk_enable @ 0x44010030
   - PSRAM chip IDs: 0x8D09=8MB (APS6408L), 0x8D08=16MB (APS128XXO), 0x1C8F=4MB (W955D8MKY)
   - PSRAM mode register values: MODE6=0xD8054041 (APS6408L), MODE7=0xD8054049 (APS128XXO), MODE8=0xB0054045 (W955D8MKY)
   - NuttX builtin app registration requires apps/examples/ directory structure (Kconfig, CMakeLists.txt, Make.defs, Makefile)
   - repack.py packages nuttx.bin into Beken flashable image with linear CRC

3. Files and Code Sections:

     - Register definitions for PSRAM controller (0x46080000 base), system analog registers, chip IDs, mode values, drive strengths

     - psram_init_aps6408l(), psram_init_aps128xxo(), psram_init_w955d8mky() - full chip init with MR configuration
     - bk7258_psram_init() - 8-step init sequence (voltage→LDO→AHB→clock→clock gate→reset→detect→default clock)
     - bk7258_psram_probe() - init + single-word data path test
     - bk7258_psram_test() - address-in-address destructive test with throughput measurement
     - bk7258_psram_alias() - alias detection at 0/4MB/8MB/16MB-4K
     - bk7258_psram_width() - 8/16/32-bit access width test

    mbps = (uint64_t)size_bytes * TICK_PER_SEC / elapsed / (1024 * 1024);

       void *bk7258_psram_calloc(size_t n, size_t size);
       void  bk7258_psram_free(void *ptr);
       void  bk7258_psram_meminfo(struct mallinfo *info);   /* 或等价形式 */

       psram freeall         释放本命令分配的全部块

结论：**LCD 帧缓冲留在 SRAM（快），PSRAM 用于摄像头大缓冲（大）**。这既符合带宽实测，

130	 *   configure properly.
131	 *
132	 ****************************************************************************/
133	
134	static void ana_write(uintptr_t addr, uint32_t val)
135	{
136	  uint32_t idx = (addr - ANA_BASE) >> 2;
137	
138	  psram_putreg(val, addr);
139	
140	  while (psram_getreg(ANA_SPI_STATE_REG) & (1u << idx))
141	    {
142	    }
143	}

145	/****************************************************************************
146	 * Name: ana_rmw
147	 *
148	 * Description:
149	 *   Read-modify-write a bit field in an analog register.
150	 *   Reads the current value, clears the mask at pos, sets the new
151	 *   value, and writes via ana_write() (with SPI polling).
152	 *
153	 ****************************************************************************/
154	
155	static void ana_rmw(uintptr_t addr, int pos, uint32_t mask,
156	                    uint32_t val)
157	{
158	  uint32_t reg = psram_getreg(addr);
159	
160	  reg &= ~(mask << pos);
161	  reg |= ((val & mask) << pos);
162	  ana_write(addr, reg);
163	}

222	/****************************************************************************
223	 * Name: psram_cmd_write
224	 *
225	 * Description:
226	 *   Write a value to a PSRAM register address via the command
227	 *   interface.  Includes a generous timeout to avoid infinite hang.
228	 *
229	 *   Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_cmd_write()
230	 ****************************************************************************/
231	
232	static int psram_cmd_write(uint32_t addr, uint32_t value)
233	{
234	  int timeout = CMD_READ_POLL_OUTER * CMD_READ_POLL_INNER;
235	
236	  psram_putreg(addr, PSRAM_LL_REG9);
237	  psram_putreg(value, PSRAM_LL_REGA);
238	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_TRIG, PSRAM_LL_REG8);
239	
240	  while ((psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REG8) & PSRAM_CMD_WRITE_TRIG) &&
241	         --timeout > 0)
242	    {
243	    }
244	
245	  if (timeout <= 0)
246	    {
247	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "psram: cmd_write timeout\n");
248	      return -ETIMEDOUT;
249	    }
250	
251	  return OK;
252	}

254	/****************************************************************************
255	 * Name: psram_cmd_read
256	 *
257	 * Description:
258	 *   Read a value from a PSRAM chip register via the command interface.
259	 *   Retries up to CMD_READ_RETRIES times, with SF reset + cmd reset
260	 *   between retries.
261	 *
262	 *   Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_cmd_read()
263	 ****************************************************************************/
264	
265	static uint32_t psram_cmd_read(uint32_t addr)
266	{
267	  int retry;
268	  int outer;
269	  int inner;
270	
271	  for (retry = 0; retry < CMD_READ_RETRIES; retry++)
272	    {
273	      psram_putreg(addr, PSRAM_LL_REG9);
274	      psram_putreg(PSRAM_CMD_READ_TRIG, PSRAM_LL_REG8);
275	
276	      for (outer = 0; outer < CMD_READ_POLL_OUTER; outer++)
277	        {
278	          for (inner = 0; inner < CMD_READ_POLL_INNER; inner++)
279	            {
280	              if (!(psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REG8) &
281	                    PSRAM_CMD_READ_TRIG))
282	                {
283	                  return psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
284	                }
285	            }
286	        }
287	
288	      /* Timeout: reset SF interface and retry */
289	
290	      psram_set_sf_reset(0);
291	      psram_set_sf_reset(1);
292	      psram_cmd_reset();
293	    }
294	
295	  return 0;
296	}

320	 * Each function configures the PSRAM controller for a specific chip
321	 * type, reads and verifies the chip ID, then configures the chip's
322	 * own mode registers (MR0/MR4/MR8) for proper latency, drive
323	 * strength, and burst settings.
324	 *
325	 * Source: Armino psram_hal.c -> psram_hal_APS6408L_init(),
326	 *         psram_hal_APS128XXO_OB9_init(),
327	 *         psram_hal_W955D8MKY_5J_init()

330	/****************************************************************************
331	 * Name: psram_init_aps6408l
332	 *
333	 * Description:
334	 *   Init sequence for AP Memory APS6408L (8MB, ID 0x8D09).
335	 *   Configures MR0 (drive/latency) and MR4 (write latency).
336	 *
337	 ****************************************************************************/
338	
339	static int psram_init_aps6408l(uint32_t *id)
340	{
341	  uint32_t val;
342	
343	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_MODE_APS6408L, PSRAM_LL_REG4);
344	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_DRV_APS6408L, PSRAM_LL_REG5);
345	  psram_cmd_reset();
346	  up_udelay(500);
347	
348	  val = psram_cmd_read(0x00000000);
349	  if (val == 0 || val != *id)
350	    {
351	      return -1;
352	    }
353	
354	  *id = val;
355	
356	  /* MR0: set drive strength and latency */
357	
358	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
359	  val = (val & ~0x1f) | (0x4 << 2) | 0x3;
360	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000000, val);
361	
362	  /* MR4: set write latency (6 @ 120 MHz) */
363	
364	  psram_cmd_read(0x00000004);
365	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
366	  val = (val & ~(0x7 << 5)) | (0x6 << 5);
367	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000004, val);
368	
369	  return 0;
370	}

377	 *   Configures MR0 (drive/latency), MR4 (write latency), and MR8
378	 *   (burst length).

380	 ****************************************************************************/

382	static int psram_init_aps128xxo(uint32_t *id)

387	  psram_putreg(PSRAM_DRV_APS128XXO, PSRAM_LL_REG5);

389	  up_udelay(500);
390	
391	  val = psram_cmd_read(0x00000000);
392	  if (val == 0 || val != *id)
393	    {
394	      return -1;
395	    }
396	
397	  *id = val;
398	
399	  /* MR0: set drive strength and latency */
400	
401	  val = psram_getreg(PSRAM_LL_REGB);
402	  val = (val & ~0x1f) | (0x6 << 2) | 0x2;
403	  psram_cmd_write(0x00000000, val);
404	
405	  /* MR4: set write latency (6 @ 120 MHz) */
406	
407	  psram_cmd_read(0x00000004);

464	/****************************************************************************
465	 * Name: bk7258_psram_init
466	 *
467	 * Description:
468	 *   Initialize the BK7258 PSRAM controller and detect the external
469	 *   PSRAM chip.  Sets g_psram_chip_id and g_psram_size.
470	 *
471	 *   Sequence (source: Armino psram_hal_power_clk_enable +
472	 *   psram_hal_config_init):
473	 *     1. Set voltage: ana_reg13 psldo_swb=1, vpsramsel=3 (1.95V)
474	 *     2. Enable PSRAM LDO: ana_reg13 enpsram=1, wait 1ms
475	 *     3. Enable AHB PSRAM power domain: clear pwd_ahbp bit
476	 *     4. Set init clock to 80 MHz (320MHz PLL, div=1)
477	 *     5. Enable PSRAM peripheral clock (bit 19)
478	 *     6. Release SF reset + set bypass bit in REG2
479	 *     7. Auto-detect: try APS6408L -> APS128XXO -> W955D8MKY
480	 *        (each: set mode/drive, reset, read ID, configure MRs)
481	 *     8. Switch to 120 MHz default clock
482	 *
483	 *   NOTE: Cache coherency not addressed (no D-cache configured).
484	 *
485	 * Returned Value:
486	 *   OK on success (chip detected), -ENODEV if no known chip found.
487	 *
488	 ****************************************************************************/
489	
490	int bk7258_psram_init(void)
491	{
492	  uint32_t val;
493	  uint32_t id;
494	
495	  g_psram_chip_id = 0;
496	  g_psram_size = 0;
497	
498	  /* Step 1: Set PSRAM LDO voltage to 1.95V (psldo_swb=1, vpsramsel=3).
499	   * Source: Armino sys_hal_psram_psldo_vset()
500	   * Must use ana_write (read-modify-write + SPI poll), not plain MMIO.
501	   */
502	
503	  ana_rmw(SYS_ANA_REG13, 28, 0x1, 1);   /* psldo_swb = 1 */
504	  ana_rmw(SYS_ANA_REG13, 29, 0x3, 3);   /* vpsramsel = 3 */
505	
506	  /* Step 2: Enable PSRAM LDO.
507	   * Source: Armino sys_hal_psram_ldo_enable()
508	   */
509	
510	  ana_rmw(SYS_ANA_REG13, 31, 0x1, 1);   /* enpsram = 1 */
511	  up_mdelay(1);
512	
513	  /* Step 3: Enable AHB PSRAM power domain.
514	   * Source: Armino bk_pm_module_vote_power_ctrl(AHBP_PSRAM, ON)
515	   *         -> sys_hal_module_power_ctrl()
516	   * Clear pwd_ahbp (bit 5) to power on the AHB domain.
517	   */
518	
519	  val = psram_getreg(SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP);
520	  val &= ~PWD_AHBP_BIT;
521	  psram_putreg(val, SYS_POWER_SLEEP_WAKEUP);
522	
523	  /* Step 4: Set init clock to 80 MHz (320 MHz PLL, divider=1).
524	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_set_clk(PSRAM_80M)
525	   */
526	
527	  psram_set_clk(0, 1);   /* sel=0 (320MHz), div=1 */
528	
529	  /* Step 5: Enable PSRAM peripheral clock (bit 19).
530	   * Source: Armino sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up(CLK_PWR_ID_PSRAM, PWR_UP)
531	   */
532	
533	  val = psram_getreg(SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE);
534	  val |= PSRAM_CKEN_BIT;
535	  psram_putreg(val, SYS_DEV_CLK_ENABLE);
536	
537	  /* Step 6: Release SF reset and set bypass bit.
538	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_config_init()
539	   */
540	
541	  psram_set_sf_reset(1);
542	  psram_set_reg2_bypass();
543	
544	  up_udelay(3000);
545	
546	  /* Step 7: Auto-detect PSRAM chip type.
547	   * Try each type in sequence; first match wins.
548	   * Each init function sets mode/drive, resets, reads ID,
549	   * and configures the chip's mode registers.
550	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_config_init()
551	   */
552	
553	  id = PSRAM_ID_APS6408L;
554	  if (psram_init_aps6408l(&id) == 0)
555	    {
556	      g_psram_chip_id = id;
557	      g_psram_size = 8 * 1024 * 1024;
558	    }
559	  else
560	    {
561	      id = PSRAM_ID_APS128XXO;
562	      if (psram_init_aps128xxo(&id) == 0)
563	        {
564	          g_psram_chip_id = id;
565	          g_psram_size = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
566	        }
567	      else
568	        {
569	          id = PSRAM_ID_W955D8MKY;
570	          if (psram_init_w955d8mky(&id) == 0)
571	            {
572	              g_psram_chip_id = id;
573	              g_psram_size = 4 * 1024 * 1024;
574	            }
575	          else
576	            {
577	              syslog(LOG_ERR,
578	                     "psram: no known chip detected\n");
579	              return -ENODEV;
580	            }
581	        }
582	    }
583	
584	  /* Step 8: Switch to 120 MHz default clock.
585	   * Source: Armino psram_hal_set_default_clk()
586	   */
587	
588	  up_mdelay(1);
589	  psram_set_clk(1, 1);   /* sel=1 (480MHz), div=1 -> 120MHz */
590	
591	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
592	         "psram: init OK, ID=0x%04x, size=%lu KB\n",
593	         g_psram_chip_id,
594	         (unsigned long)(g_psram_size / 1024));
595	  return OK;
596	}

624	/****************************************************************************
625	 * Name: bk7258_psram_probe
626	 *
627	 * Description:
628	 *   Full S1 verification: init + ID check + single-word data path
629	 *   test on the memory-mapped window (0x60000000).
630	 *
631	 *   The ID check uses the command-register path (REG9/REG_A/REG_B).
632	 *   The data path test uses the AXI memory-mapped window.  These are
633	 *   two independent hardware paths; testing both in S1 ensures we
634	 *   don't mix up "controller works" with "data window works".
635	 *
636	 *   NOTE: Cache coherency not addressed (no D-cache configured).
637	 *
638	 * Returned Value:
639	 *   OK on success, negative errno on failure.
640	 *
641	 ****************************************************************************/
642	
643	int bk7258_psram_probe(void)
644	{
645	  volatile uint32_t *psram_base;
646	  uint32_t save;
647	  uint32_t readback;
648	  int ret;
649	
650	  /* Run full init sequence */
651	
652	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
653	  if (ret < 0)
654	    {
655	      return ret;
656	    }
657	
658	  /* Single-word data path test on memory-mapped window */
659	
660	  psram_base = (volatile uint32_t *)0x60000000;
661	
662	  /* Save original content (avoid destructive test on first word) */
663	
664	  save = *psram_base;
665	
666	  /* Write test pattern */
667	
668	  *psram_base = 0xdeadbeef;
669	  readback = *psram_base;
670	
671	  /* Restore original content */
672	
673	  *psram_base = save;
674	
675	  if (readback != 0xdeadbeef)
676	    {
677	      syslog(LOG_ERR, "psram: data path FAIL "
678	             "(wrote 0xdeadbeef, read 0x%08lx)\n",
679	             (unsigned long)readback);
680	      return -EIO;
681	    }
682	
683	  syslog(LOG_INFO, "psram: data path OK (0x60000000 verified)\n");
684	  return OK;
685	}

687	/****************************************************************************
688	 * Name: bk7258_psram_test
689	 *
690	 * Description:
691	 *   Address-in-address destructive test over the PSRAM window.
692	 *   Writes each 32-bit address's own address as the value, then
693	 *   reads back and verifies.  Reports errors, throughput, and
694	 *   boundary checks.
695	 *
696	 *   WARNING: This is a destructive test.  All data in the tested
697	 *   range will be overwritten.
698	 *
699	 * Input Parameters:
700	 *   size_bytes - Number of bytes to test (rounded down to 4-byte
701	 *                alignment).  If 0, uses g_psram_size.
702	 *
703	 * Returned Value:
704	 *   OK on success (zero errors), -EIO if any mismatch found.
705	 *
706	 ****************************************************************************/
707	
708	int bk7258_psram_test(uint32_t size_bytes)
709	{
710	  volatile uint32_t *base = (volatile uint32_t *)0x60000000;
711	  volatile uint32_t *last;
712	  uint32_t errors = 0;
713	  uint32_t first_bad = 0;
714	  uint32_t first_exp = 0;
715	  uint32_t first_got = 0;
716	  uint32_t save_last;
717	  uint32_t i;
718	  uint32_t nwords;
719	  clock_t start;
720	  clock_t elapsed;
721	  uint32_t mbps;
722	  int ret;
723	
724	  ret = bk7258_psram_init();
725	  if (ret < 0)
726	    {
727	      return ret;
728	    }
729	
730	  if (size_bytes == 0)
731	    {
732	      size_bytes = g_psram_size;
733	    }
734	
735	  if (size_bytes > g_psram_size)
736	    {
737	      size_bytes = g_psram_size;
738	    }
739	
740	  nwords = size_bytes / 4;
741	
742	  syslog(LOG_INFO,
743	         "psram test: range 0x%08lx - 0x%08lx (%lu KB, destructive)\n",
744	         (unsigned long)0x60000000,
745	         (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + size_bytes - 1),
746	         (unsigned long)(size_bytes / 1024));
747	
748	  /* Write phase: each word gets its own byte address */
749	
750	  start = clock_systime_ticks();
751	
752	  for (i = 0; i < nwords; i++)
753	    {
754	      base[i] = (uint32_t)(0x60000000 + i * 4);
755	
756	      /* Progress every 1 MB */
757	
758	      if ((i & 0x3ffff) == 0 && i > 0)
759	        {
760	          syslog(LOG_INFO, "  wrote %lu MB\n",
761	                 (unsigned long)(i * 4 / (1024 * 1024)));
762	        }
763	    }
764	
765	  /* Read-and-verify phase */
766	
767	  for (i = 0; i < nwords; i++)
768	    {
769	      uint32_t expected = (uint32_t)(0x60000000 + i * 4);
770	      uint32_t actual = base[i];
771	
772	      if (actual != expected)
773	        {
774	          if (errors == 0)
775	            {
776	              first_bad = 0x60000000 + i * 4;
777	              first_exp = expected;
778	              first_got = actual;
779	            }
780	
781	          errors++;
782	
783	          /* Print first few errors in detail */
784	
785	          if (errors <= 5)
786	            {
787	              syslog(LOG_ERR,
788	                     "  MISMATCH @ 0x%08lx: "
789	                     "expected 0x%08lx, got 0x%08lx\n",
790	                     (unsigned long)(0x60000000 + i * 4),
791	                     (unsigned long)expected,
792	                     (unsigned long)actual);
793	            }
794	        }
795	
796	      /* Progress every 1 MB */
797	
798	      if ((i & 0x3ffff) == 0 && i > 0)
